suite.calibration_note: 33 benchmarks with a per-field right or wrong answer (ToolRet, BRIGHT, RouterBench and ForecastBench excluded), each weighted equally; a 1-in-6 sample of requests; confidence is the probability placed on the chosen option.

categories.label: Knowledge & Reasoning
categories.description: Academic knowledge, commonsense, mathematics, and code.

categories.label: Language Understanding
categories.description: Read a text and judge what it means: entailment, sentiment, sarcasm and stance.

categories.label: Retrieval & Classification
categories.description: Pick the right item from a large set: rank documents and products by relevance, route a message to one of many intents, sort out spam and phishing.

categories.label: Tools & Automation
categories.description: Tool choice, model routing, household control, and browser or simulator actions.

categories.label: Arts & Human Judgment
categories.description: Poetry, music, humor, human preferences, and forecasting.

categories.label: Games & Strategy
categories.description: Move selection, spatial planning, rules, and decisions against other players.

1.explainer: Choose which supplied tools are needed for a request. Tests tool selection, not arguments or execution.

2.explainer: Rank candidate tools by relevance to a user request after an initial keyword search.

3.explainer: Choose the next API to call from 53 tools using the conversation and earlier tool results.

4.explainer: Identify the intent of a banking support message, such as a failed transfer or a missing card.

5.explainer: Classify a request into 150 assistant intents, or recognize that it is outside the supported scope.

6.explainer: Route a prompt to a model to maximize measured quality or balance quality with cost.

9.explainer: Translate a household command into device decisions. A request passes only if every required field is correct.

10.explainer: Infer the user's current intent from a service dialogue. The service is supplied; this track evaluates SGD, not SGD-X or slot extraction.

11.explainer: Read a contract and decide whether each of 17 legal statements is supported, contradicted, or unstated.

12.explainer: Decide whether a claim follows from, conflicts with, or is neutral to a premise designed to fool inference models.

20.explainer: Distinguish an original limerick from a perturbed version of a poem. This tests sensitivity to poetry structure, not aesthetic taste.

21.explainer: Choose the funnier of two edited news headlines, using human humor ratings as the answer key.

22.explainer: Recognize the annotated chord at a beat from symbolic musical notes, across 129 pitch-class categories.

23.explainer: Predict which color palette a person preferred, using their earlier ratings and the palettes' RGB values.

24.explainer: Answer four-choice questions across 57 academic subjects, from history and law to science and medicine.

25.explainer: Answer 198 graduate-level science questions in physics, chemistry, and biology, with four options each.

26.explainer: Answer the easier split of school science multiple-choice questions.

27.explainer: Answer the more difficult split of school science questions that simple retrieval methods struggle with.

28.explainer: Use commonsense context to choose which of two words correctly completes an ambiguous sentence.

29.explainer: Choose the most plausible continuation of an everyday scene from four candidate endings.

30.explainer: Solve grade-school arithmetic word problems by selecting a numeric answer from four or ten choices.

31.explainer: Choose the highest-valued legal chess move using published reference values. All legal moves are offered and ties count.

32.explainer: Combine clues across long narratives to solve murder mysteries, track objects, or allocate people to teams.

33.explainer: Select every correct answer to a question. The entire answer set must match; partial selections do not pass.

34.explainer: Answer deceptively simple commonsense and trick questions. Only the ten public examples are evaluated here.

36.explainer: Rank documents that answer reasoning-intensive queries, within a candidate pool retrieved by keyword search.

37.explainer: Judge whether a product is an exact match, substitute, complement, or irrelevant to a shopping query.

38.explainer: Identify which aspect-and-sentiment combinations appear in a review. Every combination must be right for the review to pass.

39.explainer: Judge the sentiment expressed toward a specified company or financial entity in a document.

40.explainer: Decide whether a single English text is sarcastic, scored with F1 for the sarcastic class. Headline track; the Arabic and paired-text tracks are listed under each result.

41.explainer: Classify a text's stance toward a supplied topic as supportive, opposed, or neutral.

42.explainer: Determine whether clinical-trial report sections support or contradict a statement, including deliberately altered statements.

43.explainer: Predict a short Python function's output by selecting among candidate values drawn from prior model generations.

44.explainer: Answer yes/no questions about statistical association, intervention, and counterfactuals from supplied causal information.

45.explainer: Answer the text-only multiple-choice subset of expert-level Humanity's Last Exam. Images and free-response questions are excluded.

48.explainer: Assign probabilities to events resolved in July–September 2026 using frozen earlier context. Lower Brier loss is better.

50.explainer: Choose the consensus statement a human discussion group preferred, based on members' views and their recorded rankings.

51.explainer: Answer elementary-science questions from four original choices, without the supporting fact.

52.explainer: Answer everyday commonsense questions from five original choices.

53.explainer: Judge a support ticket for queue, anger and priority, against deliberately noisy labels.

54.explainer: Judge generated emails as phishing across four difficulty tiers, from obvious to misleading.

55.explainer: Detect spam in real emails, scored on the structured-focus question wording.

56.explainer: Judge whether an email and its links are malicious, scored on the main verdict.

summary_notes: Metrics exclude failed/incomplete cases; coverage is explicit. No silent replacement of failures.
Different primary metrics are not averaged across benchmarks.
Latency includes HTTPS and concurrent service scheduling; not isolated model inference.
Full raw HTTP responses/payloads and all retry timings are in http-attempts.jsonl.
BPoMP/RouterBench/GSM8K and chunked tasks retain all linked requests for sampled cases.
